title: A leak check needs a calibrated solver
statement: Calibrate a leak check's blind solver, which answers without the text, on items known to leak and items known to be clean before trusting its leak rate.
example: Under a stronger solver, only 20 of 95 items that a weaker one had passed still held.
detail: Re-run through a stronger blind solver, still from another model family, only 20 (21%) of 95 items that a weaker solver had passed survived, and 75 leaked (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0235-g5-course-build-pipeline-2026-06-23-to-06-30.qmd`). The opposite failure came from a solver that role-played test-taking tricks: it guessed from option-length and wording tells and returned blind accuracy of 1.0 on items that needed the passage, and once it was swapped for a solver that answered unknown, the same judge certified those items clean (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0096-fable-vs-haiku-strictness-audit-2026-07-09.qmd`). That audit concluded that blind-solve calibration matters more than which judge is used, and that a solver able to bluff without the passage inflates leak rates. A solver that bluffs from world knowledge flags items that do need the text, and a weak or abstaining one clears items a test-wise student would crack by option length or wording.
against: real students include test-wise ones and ones willing to click through or guess (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0092-student-ready-criticism-framework-2026-07-09.qmd`, lines 25-27), so a solver that never guesses can understate the risk. The audit itself says it does not prove its new baseline is the only correct one (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0096-fable-vs-haiku-strictness-audit-2026-07-09.qmd`), and an exact blind answer still counts as a leak whatever confidence the solver reports (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0120-rivers-demo-unit-live-2026-07-13.qmd`).
